title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools (People Ops Guide)
author: Samantha Liu
summary: Consolidated People Ops handbook entry describing Redwood culture, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding process, and practical guidance for internal tools and access requests.
content:
Overview

Purpose: This People Ops guide is a single-source reference for employees and managers on working at Redwood. It covers culture and expectations; role families and career ladder guidance; a concise benefits and perks summary; the standardized hiring and new-hire onboarding process; and a practical internal tools and access guide.

Audience
- New hires and candidates evaluating Redwood
- Managers preparing promotion packets and 30/60/90 plans
- People Ops, recruiting partners, and hiring managers
- Any employee needing access to core internal systems

1) Working at Redwood	Culture & Day-to-Day Expectations
- Mission and values: Build a reliable, production-grade inference platform. Prioritize users and operational excellence.
- Communication norms: asynchronous-first (clear PRs, issue descriptions), weekly manager 1:1s, and quarterly OKR reviews.
- Hours and collaboration: core overlap hours 10:00-16:00 PT for cross-functional work. Teams may adopt local adjustments for APAC/EMEA.
- Feedback and growth: expect continuous feedback; one documented career conversation per quarter is standard.

2) Roles & Career Ladders (summary)
- Role families: Engineering (Frontend, Backend, Serving Runtime, SRE, Infra), Product, Research/Applied ML, Design, People Ops, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Security.
- Level bands: IC1/IC2 (junior), IC3 (mid), IC4 (senior), IC5 (staff), IC6+ (principal/architect). Manager bands: M1-M4 (first-line to executive managers).

Career ladder snapshot
- IC2: Contributes to team goals, owns small features end-to-end, receives regular mentoring.
- IC3: Independently delivers complex features, influences team design, mentors peers.
- IC4: Technical leader across teams, defines implementation standards, responsible for service health and reliability outcomes.
- IC5: Sets architecture and strategy for large subsystems, leads cross-functional initiatives, recognized across the company.
- Manager progression (M1-M4): Based on people scope, operational cadence, and delivery/accountability.

Promotion rubric (what to document)
1. Impact: measurable outcomes (e.g., latency/cost improvements, customer adoption, successful rollouts).
2. Scope: systems and stakeholder breadth.
3. Craft: technical depth, design quality, and operational ownership.
4. Leadership: mentorship, hiring interview contributions, cross-team influence.
5. Communication: clear written proposals, decisions, and effective postmortems.

Promotion process (high level)
1. Candidate assembles promotion packet: summary, artifacts, metrics, and peer feedback.
2. Manager endorsement with growth plan is added.
3. Packet submitted to People Ops promotions committee.
4. Committee reviews, calibrates, and communicates decision; aim for feedback within two weeks.

3) Benefits & Perks (concise summary)
- Healthcare: employer-subsidized medical, dental, and vision (US plans include HSA/FSA options).
- Time off: baseline 20 days PTO plus public holidays; parental leave: 16 weeks paid for primary caregivers.
- Compensation & equity: annual compensation review window in Q1; managers have published target bands.
- Learning & development: $2,500 annual learning stipend and conference budget (manager approval required).
- Remote & hardware support: monthly remote stipend and flexible hardware budget for role needs.
- Wellbeing & culture: monthly wellbeing stipend, offsites, and recognition awards.

Benefit FAQ
- Enrollment: use the benefits portal (invite emailed within 30 days of start).
- International hires: People Ops provides region-specific statutory benefit details.
- Parental leave: coordinate with People Ops and your manager at least eight weeks before planned leave when possible.

4) Hiring & Onboarding Overview
Hiring process (standardized flow)
1. Requisition approval by hiring manager and finance.
2. Sourcing and interview scheduling.
3. Interview loop: recruiter screen, hiring manager screen, role-specific assessment, cross-functional interviews, compensation and reference checks.
4. Offer extended by People Ops; standard offer response window is 72 hours unless otherwise noted.

Inclusive hiring guidance
- Use structured rubrics for all interviewers and provide concrete, role-focused evaluation.
- Interview feedback is required within 48 hours of interview completion.

New hire onboarding (30/60/90 overview)
- Pre-start: People Ops completes equipment order and initial access requests (Okta/GitHub/Slack).
- Day 1: People Ops orientation, IT setup, manager 1:1 to review 30/60/90 and immediate priorities.
- Week 1 goals: complete core trainings, meet cross-functional partners, and get a high-level product/architecture demo.
- 30-day goals: own and ship a small ticket or bug fix, complete security/compliance training.
- 60-day goals: lead a small feature or meaningful improvement and present learnings.
- 90-day goals: deliver measurable impact and complete a documented career goals conversation with your manager.

Onboarding checklist (essential steps)
1. Confirm hardware receipt and VPN connectivity.
2. Sign in to Slack, Okta, Notion, and GitHub.
3. Join team channels and introduce yourself on #introductions.
4. Complete required compliance trainings in the learning portal.
5. Schedule recurring 1:1s with your manager and assigned mentor.

5) Internal Tools Guide	Owners & Access Flows
Introduction: The most commonly used systems at Redwood and how to request access. If you need help, open a People Ops ticket or post in #it-help.

Tool matrix (owner | access notes)
- Slack | Owner: Eng-DevEx | Access: provisioned via Okta SSO; if not available, request in #it-help.
- Okta | Owner: Security | Access: People Ops provisions onboarding accounts; use SSO to access other apps.
- GitHub (org) | Owner: Eng-DevEx | Access: request via GitHub access form; approvals by team leads.
- Linear | Owner: Eng-DevEx | Access: team admins invite; use Linear <> GitHub linking for PR tracking.
- Notion | Owner: Eng-DevEx | Access: People Ops provisions workspace access; request page-level permissions as needed.
- GCP Console & Projects | Owner: Eng-Infra | Access: submit IAM request via internal GCP access form; least-privilege principle enforced.
- Datadog | Owner: Eng-Platform | Access: request via #monitoring with justification and expected SLA.
- Sentry | Owner: Eng-Platform | Access: request via #platform-ops for error tracing and alerting.
- CI/CD (Buildkite/Jenkins) | Owner: Eng-Infra | Access: requires GitHub team membership and SSH key setup; onboarding checklist includes pipeline access.
- HR/Payroll Portal | Owner: People Ops | Access: invitation sent via email during onboarding window.

Access request flow (step-by-step)
1. Confirm required tool and permission with your manager.
2. Open an access ticket in People Ops or use the form linked in Notion.
3. Owner team reviews and approves (typical SLA: 2 business days).
4. Validate access and notify your manager.

Quick troubleshooting commands & links
- VPN test: curl -I https://internal.redwood/api/health (replace base URL with assigned environment).
- GitHub SSH test: ssh -T git@github.com.
- Datadog dashboards: links are available on team Notion pages under "Dashboards & Alerts."

6) Manager & Mentor Responsibilities
- Managers: set clear goals, provide quarterly feedback, sponsor promotions, and ensure a healthy onboarding experience.
- Mentors: orient new hires to the codebase, review early PRs, and introduce key cross-functional contacts.

7) FAQ & Common Policies
- Work hours: flexible; communicate extended time off and update shared calendars.
- Security: MFA required; laptops must use disk encryption.
- Expenses: submit within 30 days via expense portal with receipts and manager approval.

8) Ownership & Escalation
- Document owner: People Ops (Samantha Liu).
- Escalation contact: people-ops@redwood.ai for policy clarifications or urgent onboarding issues.

Appendix	Promotion evidence examples
- Latency improvement example: "Reduced inference p50 from 120ms to 85ms for endpoint X measured by Datadog saved query dd-query-123."
- Cost optimization example: "Implemented batching and caching that reduced token cost by 18% for workload Y."
- Reliability example: "Authored runbook and on-call rotation for service Z, reducing MTTR from 40m to 12m."
